source.book: 《史记》卷一百二十六《滑稽列传》
source.excerpt: 二世立，又欲漆其城。優旃曰：「善。主上雖無言，臣固將請之。漆城雖於百姓愁費，然佳哉！漆城蕩蕩，寇來不能上。即欲就之，易為漆耳，顧難為蔭室。」於是二世笑之，以其故止。居無何，二世殺死，優旃歸漢，數年而卒。
source.transcriptionNote: 复用现有已录入批次的逐字原文快照；底本定位、原件哈希及行号保留。电子本尚不宣称纸本异文全校。

panels.title: 要给城墙涂漆
panels.caption: 秦二世提出，要给城墙涂上漆。
panels.scene: Young emperor in black gestures toward distant UNPAINTED city wall seen from palace veranda; a closed lacquer jar sits on table as proposed material only.

panels.title: 优旃先赞成
panels.caption: 优旃说：“好啊！您不说，我本来也想提这件事。”
panels.scene: Short adult You Zhan bows lightly and gives an apparently approving gesture; emperor looks pleased.

evidence.excerpt: 主上雖無言，臣固將請之

panels.title: 话里有话
panels.caption: “给城墙涂漆，百姓虽然要愁苦破费，可真是好看啊！”
panels.scene: You Zhan gestures toward one small lacquer pot and a scale wooden wall model on table, expression wry but respectful. Real city remains unpainted.

evidence.excerpt: 漆城雖於百姓愁費，然佳哉

panels.title: 还有个好处
panels.caption: “墙面滑溜溜的，敌人来了，也爬不上去！”
panels.scene: You Zhan demonstrates smooth surface using the same SMALL TABLETOP wall model and a tiny wooden ladder. All imagined military effects remain a model illustration, no real attack.

panels.title: 难在晾干
panels.caption: “漆倒容易找，只是晾漆的阴凉大屋，到哪里找得下整座城呢？”
panels.scene: You Zhan gestures widely above small model to indicate an impossibly huge drying shed; no shed is actually built. Emperor expression changes from surprise to amusement.

panels.title: 一笑作罢
panels.caption: 秦二世笑了，给城墙涂漆的计划也就停了下来。
panels.scene: Final palace scene: emperor laughs and waves away the plan, lacquer jar remains closed, distant city wall still entirely unpainted, You Zhan smiles gently.

evidence.excerpt: 於是二世笑之，以其故止

adaptations: 漆城没有执行；模型是明确的艺术示意，不补成真实设计会议或已施工事实。
“难为荫室”按讽谏笑话呈现，不当成现代涂装工艺说明。

checks: 逐格核对情节、人物与关键道具
直接参考用户选定的徙木立信：夸张造型、简练黑线、平涂色块
无嵌入正文，无虚构结果

generation.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: a finished Histree vintage Chinese lianhuanhua story atlas, exactly 6 sequential illustrations on ONE image. Primary request: 优旃劝阻漆城. Composition: STRICT equal rectangular grid of TWO columns and 3 rows. Read left to right, top to bottom. All row heights equal, all column widths equal. Canvas target 1024 x 960. Narrow straight cream gutters, maximum 4 pixels; no outer margin, no header/footer; every scene fills its own complete LANDSCAPE cell. No merged panels, insets, or changes in layout.
Style: classic 1950s-1960s Chinese small-picture storybook, early Shanghai Animation folk-art sensibility. Graceful expressive fine ink outlines, hand-painted gouache, mineral blue/green, muted cinnabar and ochre, textured warm cream paper, restrained humor and human facial expressions. Rich but legible environments; varied wide/medium/close shots. NOT modern anime, 3D, glossy or photorealistic. Ancient China, no modern objects. No words, letters, numbers, captions, speech balloons, calligraphy, watermark or symbols that look like writing ANYWHERE. Clothing and face continuity within the atlas is essential.
Characters and invariants: You Zhan: respectful adult man of short stature, rust-red robe, small dark cap, warm clever face, moustache, same design as rain-guards story. Qin Er Shi: young adult emperor in black robe with burgundy lining, simple ancient Qin crown, short beard. No actual painted entire city or constructed drying shed: these are ONLY a plan and a satirical explanation. If scene visualizes the idea, keep it on a small tabletop scale model with no writing; never as a completed real city.
Scenes in this exact order:
1. Young emperor in black gestures toward distant UNPAINTED city wall seen from palace veranda; a closed lacquer jar sits on table as proposed material only.
2. Short adult You Zhan bows lightly and gives an apparently approving gesture; emperor looks pleased.
3. You Zhan gestures toward one small lacquer pot and a scale wooden wall model on table, expression wry but respectful. Real city remains unpainted.
4. You Zhan demonstrates smooth surface using the same SMALL TABLETOP wall model and a tiny wooden ladder. All imagined military effects remain a model illustration, no real attack.
5. You Zhan gestures widely above small model to indicate an impossibly huge drying shed; no shed is actually built. Emperor expression changes from surprise to amusement.
6. Final palace scene: emperor laughs and waves away the plan, lacquer jar remains closed, distant city wall still entirely unpainted, You Zhan smiles gently.

styleRefinement.instructions: Use case: style-transfer. Restyle ONLY IMAGE 1, the edit target. IMAGE 2 (approved older 移木立信 artwork) is the PRIMARY style reference; IMAGE 3 (newly corrected fish-refusal artwork) is a SECONDARY reference for the same approved style. Do not import reference story events, characters, sword/pole/fish props, captions or text. Draw the target in the same artistic language as images 2 and 3: strongly designed Chinese folk/early Shanghai animation characters, larger expressive heads, compact stylized adult bodies, angular expressive eyebrows and noses made with very few confident strokes, small curved eyes, humorous expressive poses, fluid varied BLACK ink contours, FLAT matte pigment blocks with only spare broad ink-wash texture. Reduce realistic anatomy, skin modeling, facial shading, brocade patterns, tiny clothing folds and detailed background rendering dramatically. Robes are mostly solid muted color fields with spare trim, NO all-over elaborate embroidery. Simplify background buildings into rhythmic geometric silhouettes, light ink washes and warm UNPAINTED cream space. Restrained indigo, ochre and cinnabar, subtle paper grain like image 2, no dense brown texture overlay. NOT realistic illustrated portraiture, glossy painting, modern anime, chibi toys, 3D or photorealism. Keep all characters ADULT unless explicitly elderly. Preserve each character's consistent identifying robe color, beard and role, but redraw their form in this stylized way. No words, numerals, letters, title, captions, calligraphy, speech bubbles, watermark or readable marks ANYWHERE, including on documents, garments or props. Ignore all text visible in the style reference. Do not add a header or footer.

previousAfterword.title: 顺着说，才听出荒唐
paragraphs: 优旃先顺着秦二世的想法，把“好处”越说越大，最后用难找晾漆大屋的笑话点出计划的荒唐。
《史记》记的是计划被劝止，没有说城墙已经涂完漆。画面中的小模型只是帮助理解对白的艺术表现。

takeaway.title: 把想法往下推一步
takeaway.text: 听上去漂亮的计划，也要想想实际怎样完成。

previousAfterword.sourceNote: 据《史记》卷一百二十六《滑稽列传》改编。对白为现代白话改写，人物外貌、动作细节和现场构图为艺术表现。
